about.title: Fresno Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Fresno sits where SR-41 and SR-99 cross, and much of the city's traffic funnels through those two highways or along Blackstone and Shaw Avenues. Public collision records for 2025 show 1,629 injury crashes inside the city, with 2,186 people hurt and 53 lives lost. Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. account for the largest share of reports, which lines up with the end-of-week commute across Fresno County. If one of those collisions involved you, the days that follow can feel scattered. Medical appointments pile up, an adjuster calls before you've had a chance to think, and the car sits somewhere waiting on an estimate. LawProactive exists to take one item off that list. We're not a law firm. We connect you, at no charge, with an independent Fresno-area attorney who handles car accident claims on contingency. You pay a fee only if there's a recovery. Before you speak with the other driver's insurer, it helps to have someone who knows California's pure comparative fault rules and two-year filing window in your corner.

whyChoose.title: Why Fresno Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: The clock is shorter than it looks
items.desc: California gives you two years to file a car accident lawsuit, but if a city vehicle, Caltrans truck or other public agency was involved, a claim may need to be submitted in as little as six months. An attorney can sort out which deadline applies to your crash.

items.title: Partial fault doesn't shut you out
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you were partly to blame for a Fresno collision; your share is simply reduced by your percentage of fault. The other insurer will try to push that percentage up, which is why early guidance matters.

items.title: No fee unless you recover
items.desc: Every attorney in our network works on contingency, so there's nothing to pay up front and no fee at all unless money is recovered. California also places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and lost enjoyment of life in ordinary car accident cases.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You're not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and it's usually wise to hold off. Adjusters ask questions designed to lock in details that can later be used to raise your share of fault under California's comparative negligence rule. Speaking with an attorney first lets you understand what you're agreeing to before anything is on tape.

items.question: I was hit on SR-99 near downtown Fresno. Does it matter that it happened on a state highway?
items.answer: The location can affect who is responsible and how long you have to act. If a road defect, missing signage or a government-owned vehicle played a role, a claim against Caltrans or the City of Fresno may need to be filed within six months rather than the usual two years. An attorney can review the police report and determine whether any public entity belongs in your claim.

items.question: What should I save from the crash while I wait to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: Keep everything: photos of both vehicles and the roadway, the CHP or Fresno Police report number, medical discharge papers, receipts, and the names of anyone who saw what happened. Don't repair or dispose of your car until the damage has been documented. If a dash cam or nearby business camera captured the collision, note it right away, since that footage is often overwritten within days.
